keyImprovements: Names the current MLB parent model as MLB-M0 so future changes can be compared against a stable baseline.

Adds a May 30 closeout gate so side predictions must flow into `mlb_side_predictions` and `mlb_side_backtests` before postmortem lessons are trusted.
Adds a cartridge-local performance index and quiet-start full-game gate so May 30 failures can affect the next slate instead of staying as notes.

Moves MLB-M0 workflows and publish lanes into the cartridge while old pipeline paths remain compatibility launchers.
Adds a documented pipeline ownership boundary so data plumbing and offline research are not mistaken for missed model code.
Adds a component registry for sides, first-five, totals, props, HRs, market context, and MLB-RP36 so future work can land in the right model lane without scanning the whole cartridge.
Indexes MLB-M0 and MLB-RP36 run snapshots into shared warehouse model-run tables so performance/backtest queries no longer depend only on JSON files.
Adds registry-aware MLB lifecycle wrappers so future parent models can be scaffolded, run, snapshotted, checked, and compared without hardcoding package scripts to MLB-M0.
Adds an app adapter registry so future active parent models must register their app-facing contract instead of silently rendering through MLB-M0.

modelDescription.name: MLB-M2 game-shape reality-gap branch
modelDescription.summary: Active-inspection MLB parent cartridge promoted from MLB-M0 on 2026-06-01. M2 keeps the M0 app and publish contracts, then adds a game-shape/reality-gap layer that asks whether the side, total, first-five, and first-inning reads match the way the game is likely to unfold.
keyImprovements: Promotes a full parent cartridge from MLB-M0 for live slate inspection while preserving M0 as the baseline comparison target.
Adds `analysis.gameShape`, a structured read of phase agreement, crooked-inning chaos, dead-early shape, bullpen-flip risk, and projection-vs-reality gap.
Adds an RF research lens that treats RandomForest results as a nonlinear reality check, with totals as the only currently deployable RF lane from the research docs.
Keeps ML/F5 RF influence downgraded until bucketed backtests show it beats the current M0 logic.
Names market implications separately for side, first-five, total, and first inning so M2 can stop forcing moneyline when the game shape says another lane is cleaner.
Adds concrete game-shape categories, lane maps, and inning maps so the site can explain starter windows, bridge innings, crooked-inning exposure, and live-entry requirements.

keyMetrics.details: M2 category lane hit on 195 graded rows from 2026-05-10 through 2026-05-31; baseline full-game side was 59.0% on 212 rows.

keyMetrics.label: Warehouse coverage
keyMetrics.details: May 31 M2 derived tables pass freshness and minimum-row checks for state formulas, player identity, pitcher-batter kernel, and backtests.

notes: M2 is now active for inspection, not a promise that RF is better. It is the branch where RF impact can finally be measured instead of hand-waved.
The core question is whether the model can describe game flow before choosing a bet: early scoring, first-five control, bridge innings, total chaos, and conversion failure.
A high reality-gap score should downgrade blind full-game ML confidence even when the raw side model has a strong lean.
The transparent category layer beat the tested walk-forward RF, gradient, and logistic lane choosers overall; the ML experiments only helped narrow F5/high-total sublanes.
Rule sweeps surfaced useful candidate gates: starter-control rows for full-game side, phase-split rows for F5, and high-chaos rows for total/first-inning scoring shape.
Future M2 work should persist per-game reality-gap outcomes so we can backtest whether high-gap labels predicted bad ML bets, better F5 bets, better totals, or passes.
The value board is now treated as a publish contract: the UI can filter/sort, but it cannot invent first-five or totals EV from raw projections.
knownLimitations: The RF lens currently uses documented research baselines, not a newly serialized production RF artifact.
M2 was promoted by operator request for live inspection before it fully beat the baseline; risky lanes must remain visibly gated.
The first game-shape formula is intentionally transparent and testable; it still needs day-by-day settlement to prove lift.

modelDescription.name: MLB-M0 parent baseline
modelDescription.summary: Baseline MLB parent cartridge. MLB-M0 owns the daily workflow surface, publish lanes, MLB-specific scoring adapters, run manifest, closeout health gate, and the MLB-RP36 relief addendum boundary. Model-neutral sports plumbing now lives in models/shared/sports-core. Remaining pipeline files are source fetchers, warehouse commands, compatibility launchers, or offline research until a future model promotes them.
keyImprovements: Names the current MLB parent model as MLB-M0 so future changes can be compared against a stable baseline.
Keeps MLB-RP36 as a relief addendum consumed by MLB-M0 instead of treating the reliever shadow artifact as a separate parent model.

Adds a cartridge-local performance index and quiet-start full-game gate so May 30 failures can affect the next slate instead of staying as notes.
Persists daily hitter platoon split snapshots so the prop model can be audited against the exact split context shown pregame.

Moves MLB-M0 workflows and publish lanes into the cartridge while old pipeline paths remain compatibility launchers.
Adds a documented pipeline ownership boundary so data plumbing and offline research are not mistaken for missed model code.
Adds a component registry for sides, first-five, totals, props, HRs, market context, and MLB-RP36 so future work can land in the right model lane without scanning the whole cartridge.

Adds registry-aware MLB lifecycle wrappers so future parent models can be scaffolded, run, snapshotted, checked, and compared without hardcoding package scripts to MLB-M0.
Adds an app adapter registry so future active parent models must register their app-facing contract instead of silently rendering through MLB-M0.

Routes MLB-RP36 package scripts and refresh consumption through registry-aware component wrappers.
